title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit
plain: There's an electrical problem with fuel temperature sensor A. The computer uses fuel temperature to fine-tune how much fuel it injects, mainly on diesels and some gas engines.
symptoms: Possible hard starting or slight drop in power
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare the fuel temperature reading with other temperature sensors on a cold engine
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the fuel temperature sensor.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
plain: Fuel temperature sensor A is giving readings that don't make sense compared with the engine's other temperature sensors.

causes.name: Corroded connector or high wiring resistance
Fuel overheating from a fuel cooler or return problem

checks: Compare fuel, coolant and intake air temperatures after the car sits overnight
Inspect the connector for corrosion
fix: Usually a new fuel temperature sensor or a connector repair.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
plain: Fuel temperature sensor A is reporting an impossibly hot reading, which usually means a shorted wire or failed sensor.
checks: Unplug the sensor and see if the reading drops to a very cold value
Inspect the wiring for pinched or rubbed spots
fix: Repair the shorted wiring or replace the fuel temperature sensor.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
plain: Fuel temperature sensor A is reporting an impossibly cold reading, usually because it is unplugged, a wire is broken, or the sensor has failed.
checks: Check that the sensor is plugged in and the pins are clean
Look for a reading stuck near minus 40, which points to an open circuit
fix: Repair the connector or wiring, or replace the fuel temperature sensor.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
plain: Fuel temperature sensor A's reading keeps cutting out or jumping, usually from a loose connection.
checks: Wiggle-test the connector and wiring while watching the live reading
Inspect the connector pins for corrosion
fix: Repair the connection or wiring; replace the sensor if the reading still jumps.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit

symptoms: Possible hard starting or slight drop in power
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare the reading with other temperature sensors on a cold engine
fix: Repair the wiring or replace fuel temperature sensor B.

title: Fuel Pressure Sensor "B" Circuit
plain: There's an electrical problem with fuel pressure sensor B, a second fuel pressure sensor used on some engines (often on the low-pressure supply side).
symptoms: Possible hard starting or loss of power
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Check the sensor's 5-volt reference, ground and signal
fix: Repair the wiring or connector, or replace fuel pressure sensor B.

title: Fuel Pressure Sensor "B" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: Fuel pressure sensor B's readings don't match what the computer expects. The fuel pressure may really be off, or the sensor may be reading wrong.
symptoms: Possible hesitation, loss of power or hard starting

causes.name: Real fuel pressure problem such as a weak pump or clogged filter

checks: Compare the sensor reading with a mechanical fuel pressure gauge
Inspect the connector and wiring
fix: Fix the fuel supply problem, or replace the sensor if it reads wrong.

title: Fuel Pressure Sensor "B" Circuit Low
plain: Fuel pressure sensor B's signal is lower than its normal range, usually from a wiring problem or failed sensor.
symptoms: Possible hard starting or loss of power

causes.name: Signal wire open or shorted to ground, or lost 5-volt reference

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Check the sensor's 5-volt reference, ground and signal
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the sensor.

title: Fuel Pressure Sensor "B" Circuit High
plain: Fuel pressure sensor B's signal is higher than its normal range, usually from a short in the wiring, an open ground or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Possible hard starting or loss of power
checks: Inspect the sensor wiring for damage
Check the sensor ground and signal with the engine off
fix: Repair the wiring or ground, or replace the sensor.

title: Fuel Pressure Sensor "B" Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
plain: Fuel pressure sensor B's signal keeps dropping out or jumping around, usually from a loose connection or failing sensor.
symptoms: Occasional stumble or loss of power
checks: Wiggle-test the connector and wiring while watching the live reading
Inspect the connector pins for corrosion
fix: Repair the connection or wiring; replace the sensor if the signal still jumps.

title: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Frequent Activation
plain: The safety valve that bleeds off excess fuel pressure has been opening too often. Fuel pressure is spiking higher than it should, which needs attention.
symptoms: Possible loss of power or rough running

causes.name: Faulty fuel pressure control valve or regulator
Faulty fuel rail pressure sensor reading wrong
Worn or leaking pressure relief valve

checks: Compare desired and actual fuel rail pressure on a scan tool
Check for related fuel pressure sensor or regulator codes
fix: Usually a pressure control valve, rail pressure sensor or relief valve, depending on what testing shows.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit
plain: There's an electrical problem with the sensor that measures fuel pressure in the fuel rail. Diesels and direct-injection gas engines rely on it heavily, so starting and power can suffer.
symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

causes.name: Lost 5-volt reference from the engine computer

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring on the fuel rail
Check the sensor's 5-volt reference, ground and signal
Look for other codes sharing the same 5-volt reference
fix: Repair the wiring or connector, or replace the fuel rail pressure sensor.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The fuel rail pressure reading doesn't match what the computer expects. Fuel pressure may really be wrong, or the sensor may be giving bad readings.

causes.name: Real fuel pressure problem such as a weak pump or clogged filter
Faulty fuel pressure regulator or control valve

checks: Compare the sensor reading with key on, engine off to the expected value
Compare desired and actual rail pressure while driving
Check the fuel filter and supply pressure
fix: Often a new fuel rail pressure sensor; fix any real fuel supply or regulator problem first.
examples: Seen on diesels and direct-injection gas engines that run a high-pressure fuel rail

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Low
plain: The fuel rail pressure sensor's signal is lower than its normal range, usually from a wiring fault or failed sensor.

causes.name: Signal wire open or shorted to ground

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Check the sensor's 5-volt reference, ground and signal
Look for other codes sharing the same 5-volt reference
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the fuel rail pressure sensor.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit High
plain: The fuel rail pressure sensor's signal is higher than its normal range, usually from a short in the wiring, an open ground or a failed sensor.
symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode
checks: Inspect the sensor wiring for damage
Check the sensor ground and signal with the engine off
Compare the reading with key on, engine off to the expected value
fix: Repair the wiring or ground, or replace the fuel rail pressure sensor.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent
plain: The fuel rail pressure sensor's signal keeps dropping out or jumping, usually from a loose connection or failing sensor.
symptoms: Occasional stumble, stall or loss of power
checks: Wiggle-test the connector and wiring while watching the live reading
Inspect the connector pins for corrosion
fix: Repair the connection or wiring; replace the sensor if the signal still drops out.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Circuit
plain: There's an electrical problem with the engine oil temperature sensor, which some engines use to protect the engine and manage things like valve timing.
symptoms: Oil temperature gauge may read wrong
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare the oil and coolant temperature readings on a cold engine
fix: Repair the wiring or replace the oil temperature sensor.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
plain: The engine oil temperature reading doesn't make sense compared with the engine's other temperature readings.

causes.name: Corroded connector or high wiring resistance

checks: Check the engine oil level
Compare the oil and coolant temperature readings after the car sits overnight
fix: Usually a new oil temperature sensor or a connector repair.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Low
plain: The engine oil temperature sensor is reporting an impossibly hot reading, usually from a shorted wire or failed sensor. Make sure the engine isn't really overheating.
symptoms: Oil temperature gauge may read high
checks: Confirm the engine isn't really overheating and the oil level is correct
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading drops to a very cold value
fix: Repair the shorted wiring or replace the oil temperature sensor.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor High
plain: The engine oil temperature sensor is reporting an impossibly cold reading, usually because it is unplugged, a wire is broken, or the sensor has failed.
symptoms: Oil temperature gauge may stay low
checks: Check that the sensor is plugged in and the pins are clean
Look for a reading stuck near minus 40, which points to an open circuit
fix: Repair the connector or wiring, or replace the oil temperature sensor.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Intermittent
plain: The engine oil temperature reading keeps cutting out or jumping, usually from a loose connection or failing sensor.
symptoms: Oil temperature gauge may jump around
checks: Wiggle-test the connector and wiring while watching the live reading
Clean any oil out of the connector
fix: Repair the connection or wiring; replace the sensor if the reading still jumps.
